projects.name: ContextFinder.ai
projects.short: Chrome extension that summarizes academic PDFs.
projects.description: A Chrome extension that summarizes dense academic pages and PDFs (course outlines, papers) in under 5 seconds, then answers follow-up questions grounded in that document. The React + TypeScript UI is bundled with webpack and talks to a Node.js backend on Firebase that calls the Anthropic API. The fun challenge was cost: optimizing the API calls so each request stays around $0.02, with a CI/CD pipeline and a Jest suite keeping it shippable.
projects.imageAlt: ContextFinder.ai popup showing a generated summary of a SOEN 357 course outline PDF

projects.name: JumpSHREK
projects.short: Godot platformer. Won both awards at CGD Shrekathon 2026.
projects.description: A 2D platformer built in Godot (GDScript + C#) with a 5-person team for CGD Shrekathon 2026, Concordia's game jam: climb the mountain layer by layer to reach Fiona while escaping the Dragon. It has layered jump mechanics, branching routes and endings based on your choices with Puss in Boots, Donkey and Rumpelstiltskin. The trickiest part was enemy AI that watches how you play and adapts its strategy. It won both Best Game (judges) and Community Choice (participants).
projects.imageAlt: JumpSHREK gameplay: Shrek climbs the mountain while Donkey shouts "SHREK! Hallelujah, you're here!"

gallery.alt: The JumpSHREK team posing together at CGD Shrekathon 2026

projects.name: Sumo Robot
projects.description: A sumo robot built for Robowars 2026 on an ESP32-S3 (Freenove WROOM). Most of the work was embedded debugging: tracking down a dead TCA9548A I²C multiplexer that was taking the sensors behind it off the bus, and resolving GPIO pin conflicts on the board. The final firmware shipped in time for competition day.
projects.imageAlt: Max and teammates tuning the sumo robot on a laptop at Robowars 2026

projects.name: Advocato
projects.short: AI legal-argument add-on for Google Docs.
projects.description: Built with a 3-person team at the CAIJ 2nd Annual AI Integration Hackathon: a Google Docs add-on that takes a Québec lawyer from case exhibits (PDF/DOCX) to a sourced argument matrix, using live CAIJ case-law search and the Augure LLM, in French and English. To stop hallucinated citations, every LLM response is validated against Zod schemas plus a grounding check that rejects any case, fact or exhibit not found in the retrieved sources. The LLM, search and Drive sit behind swappable adapters, which made an offline demo mode and a 230-test suite possible.
projects.imageAlt: Advocato sidebar in Google Docs generating a sourced French legal argument, with unverified citations flagged

projects.name: CaffeineCrash
projects.short: 24-hour co-op zombie survival game, ConuHacks X.
projects.description: A 2D zombie survival game built in 24 hours with a 4-person team at ConuHacks X. I worked on zombie AI, scene management and player interaction in GDScript. The hard part was online co-op: syncing player state and enemy behaviour in real time over Godot's high-level multiplayer API before the clock ran out. Think COD Zombies, except every Perk-a-Cola is just Celsius.
projects.imageAlt: CaffeineCrash gameplay: a horde closing in while the Liquid Energy meter runs low

gallery.alt: The CaffeineCrash team at ConuHacks X with the game's title screen on a monitor

projects.name: WhosOnBreak
projects.short: Shift and break scheduling app for Android.
projects.description: A scheduling app for figuring out who's working, who's on break and when, with friend codes you share by QR. It's a TypeScript monorepo: an Expo / React Native Android app with a drag-and-drop week editor, and a Hono API on Cloudflare Workers backed by Neon Postgres, with Google sign-in and JWT auth. The scheduling rules (breaks, A/B week cycles, time zones) live in a dependency-free core package, and shared Zod contracts keep the app and the API agreeing on every request. Rate limiting runs on Durable Objects across all isolates, and the API tests run against PGlite (Postgres in WebAssembly), so CI needs no real database or secrets. Targeting a Google Play release with a free tier and a paid version.
projects.imageAlt: WhosOnBreak app icon: two people next to a colourful schedule chart

projects.name: LINKT
projects.description: A team-built event management platform with separate React/TypeScript frontend and Spring Boot backend modules. I designed 8+ REST endpoints for event queries, authentication and persistence. Keeping average API response time under 500 ms while reaching 90% backend test coverage was the main engineering goal.
projects.imageAlt: LINKT's Browse Events page: search, category and price filters above campus event cards

projects.name: maxingram.dev
projects.short: This site! A retro RPG portfolio.
projects.description: This site: an Undertale-inspired retro RPG portfolio served as static assets from a Cloudflare Worker. It's plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JS with no framework and no build step, and every bit of text comes from one JSON file. All the sound is synthesized live with the Web Audio API: square-wave dialogue blips and a Karplus-Strong plucked-string guitar, so there isn't a single audio file.
projects.imageAlt: maxingram.dev social preview card with Max's pixel avatar

about.bio: * Hi, I'm Max: a Software Engineering student at Concordia in Montreal, fully bilingual in English and French. I like building things you can actually use, working on projects, and participating in hackathons and game jams. When I'm not coding I'm probably out on my bike, playing guitar, or playing video games.
